defs.def: a feeling of sympathy and sadness caused by the suffering and troubles of others 同情；怜悯

ex.s: The things we learn in maturity seldom involve information and skills． We learn to bear with the things we can't change． We learn to avoid self﹣pity． We learn that however much we try to please， some people are never going to love us﹣an idea that troubles at first but is eventually relaxing．
ex.t: C．通过将遭到破坏的生态系统恢复正常。

ex.s: B．A wise man can live without self﹣pity．
ex.t: B．那些倾向于回顾过去的人几乎无法前进。

ex.s: In his first years of high school, Gabriel would look pityingly at music students,     36     across the campus with their heavy instrument cases,     37       at school for practice hours     38       anyone else had to be there.
ex.t: 结果显示红背细尾鹩莺的雏鸟也像它们的妈妈一样啾啾叫。

ex.s: When I compare myself to you, I feel an immense pity for myself, poor unfortunate monster that I am!
ex.t: 当我拿自己和你比时，我对自己感到极其的可怜，我这可怜不幸的怪物啊！

ex.s: A drop of water and a little pity — that is more than I can repay with my life.
ex.t: 一滴水和一点点怜悯——这是我用生命也无法偿还的。

ex.s: Jenny: I think it would be a great pity to pass up the opportunity to be admitted without taking the exam.
ex.t: 珍妮：我认为放弃免试录取的机会真是太可惜了。

ex.s: Robert The Road Not Taken is one of America’s best-loved poems, and I think it is a pity that it is generally misunderstood as a call for facing the future without regret.
ex.t: 罗伯特：《未选择的路》是美国最受喜爱的诗歌之一，我认为很可惜它通常被误解为是一首号召人们不留遗憾地面对未来的诗。

ex.s: Pity my camera battery was flat!
ex.t: 可惜我的相机电池没电了！
